To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the method presented in this paper allows the incipient slippages between an object and a sensor to be detected, without any knowledge of the friction coefficients, by processing the signals generated by the sensor.
the proposed method, based on the use of an artificial neural network, is able to detect incipient object slipping in the case of a skin-like sensor.

1) a neural network can be trained to detect incipient object slippoage using as input the shear stresses measured on the skin-like sensor, 2) the method does not need any priori knowledge on the friction coefficient between object and sensor, 3) it is robust to noise and 4) it is validated both by simulation and experiment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a neural network based on a skin-like tactile sensor for the detection of the insipiency in slippage.
the development of a tactile system able to detect incipient object slip.
a new method for the detection of incipient slippers based on the use of skin-like sensors and neural networks.

the method is able of learning the frictional properties of the contact and is robust to small noise.

the method is able, with a good accuracy, to predict the insipient slippage in the case of a single object.
the method is able of recognizing the incipiency of slipping between the sensor and an object in contact with it, even if the friction coefficient is not known a priori.
we have shown the possibility of using a neural network for detecting incipient slippages in a skin-like tactile sensor.

the proposed method is able to recognize the insipiency and the direction of the slippage.
